reviews.body:
this is the same guard as the older draft #9342 (resolves #9341, which #9650 duplicates, and a maintainer already asked that author if it is ready). i ran main's encoder with your `(dict, list)` check and with #9342's `hash()` check on tuple, nested, namedtuple, enum-with-list and dataclass keys: identical output on all 6, and #9342's tests also cover namedtuple/enum/nested.

one gap in both: `encode({(1, 2): "t", "(1, 2)": "s"})` now returns `{"(1, 2)": "s"}`, main kept both inside the repr string. also `frozenset({'a','b','c'})` stringifies in a different order under `PYTHONHASHSEED=1` vs `2`, so the key is not stable across runs.

(ai-assisted, checked by me)

Thanks @pcbeingused333. I renamed the title to the format the PR Linter expects and linked #9341, which is the original report of this bug. I ran it locally: tuple and frozenset keys keep the dict structure, a string key and a tuple key with the same text both survive, and frozenset keys come out the same on every run. The full SDK unit suite passes.

review_comments.body: ### Key-collision renaming behavior left undocumented Colliding stringified tuple, frozenset, or dataclass keys are silently renamed with a repeated ` []` suffix, but the current comment only covers native keys taking precedence. Document this rewrite format and when it applies. Want Baz to fix this for you? comments.body:
Merger   ✅ Ready to Merge

 MERGE: the PR delivers the tuple/frozenset key fix, and the only open finding is low severity; organizational guidelines state low-severity findings do not block approval.

Thanks for the careful look. Two gaps were real, and the new commit covers both:

- `encode({(1, 2): "t", "(1, 2)": "s"})` lost an entry, because the stringified tuple key overwrote the native `"(1, 2)"` key. Native keys are now placed first, and a stringified key that would collide gets a `" [tuple]"` suffix (type name), so both values are kept.
- `frozenset` keys were stringified in an order that depends on `PYTHONHASHSEED`. They now render as `frozenset({...})` with the elements sorted by `repr`, so the key is stable across runs.

On #9342: as far as I can tell it is a draft that has not moved since 11-02, so this PR keeps the fix going. It also adds the collision handling and the stable ordering, which are the cases that draft does not cover.

Tests added for both cases (collision test fails before, passes after; run under several PYTHONHASHSEED values).

This comment and commit were prepared with the help of an AI assistant (Claude Code) and submitted by the account owner.
